title: Short connections inside polynomial lemniscates
question: For a monic polynomial whose roots lie in the open unit disc, must two roots be joinable by a curve of length less than two inside the open unit lemniscate?
authority_posture: not_registered; the claim registry does not carry these declarations and kernel checking them does not promote them into reviewed public claims
what_is_checked: Along a trajectory tangent to the complex Newton vector field -f/f', the polynomial value satisfies w' = -w.
The exponentially rescaled polynomial value is a first integral, so the value of a Newton trajectory remains on one oriented ray.
A finite Newton-flow connection can only join endpoints whose polynomial values lie on the same positive ray; distinct critical-value arguments therefore exclude such a connection.
For two translated critical values, the ray-collision locus is a real affine line with an exact one-parameter description.
A finite family of ray-collision lines can be avoided by an arbitrarily small common translation.
An explicit root-retention estimate keeps roots of a sufficiently small constant perturbation inside the unit disc.
what_is_not_checked: The spanning-tree decomposition claimed in the March 2026 manuscript; its printed Proposition 12 proof uses an invalid three-ended local saddle block, and a Cassini example refutes the printed global tree budget.
A repair of Proposition 12 that retains the printed 1/(2π) spanning-tree coefficient; any later argument must change the metric inequality.
A perturbation theorem that first makes critical values injective while preserving the relevant lemniscate component, collars, and strict length slack.
The global planar decomposition and metric gluing needed to obtain a curve of length less than two.

open_obligations.statement: The printed 1/(2π) spanning-tree estimate of Proposition 12 is false. Any later argument must pay a positive attachment cost, select only one short pair, or use a different global metric inequality.
Build a compact strip or cell decomposition after cutting along critical-value rays, without presupposing the unproved local valence count.
Glue the local pieces with strict quantitative slack while preserving the sharp one-over-two-pi length bookkeeping.
First separate critical values, then apply the checked small translation, while retaining roots, the selected component, collars, ray separation, and a strict length margin.
Prove the global relative Newton-flow theorem that turns the checked ray separation into the required root-to-root curve inside the original open lemniscate.

finite_search: A raster search samples named failure modes through degree ten and returns candidate upper bounds only. It is finite numerical evidence, not a topology proof or a counterexample certificate.

main_results.statement: An arbitrarily small common translation separates a finite injective family from zero and from shared positive rays.
main_results.boundary: Finite-family avoidance does not provide the global topological or metric gluing.

main_results.statement: A quantified small constant perturbation keeps every polynomial root inside the open unit disc.
main_results.boundary: Root retention is only one input to an incomplete global route.

families.contribution_class: locally proved result and formalised calculus; novelty unassessed
families.summary: Lean checks the local Newton value equation and the zero-derivative form of its exponentially scaled value; constancy along a real-time interval is an ordinary calculus consequence in the paper.
families.boundary: The cited declarations are pointwise derivative statements. The real-time first integral requires the paper’s interval integration step, and value decay alone does not construct a global trajectory or give a short connecting curve.

families.summary: Lean checks that distinct positive rays contradict an assumed exponential endpoint relation; the paper derives that relation for a finite real-time Newton trajectory by ordinary integration and endpoint continuity.
families.boundary: The finite-trajectory conclusion retains continuity on the closed interval, differentiability and noncritical Newton evolution on its interior, and the ordinary endpoint passage. It supplies neither global trajectory existence nor geometric length control.

families.summary: Collision translations are parameterised by real affine lines and an arbitrarily small common translation avoids finitely many of them.
families.boundary: The finite-family avoidance theorem does not perform the global topology or metric gluing.

families.summary: A quantified small constant perturbation keeps every polynomial root inside the open unit disc.
families.boundary: Root retention is one input to a still-incomplete route.

families.summary: The paper identifies an invalid local saddle block in a claimed unrestricted proof.
families.boundary: The diagnosis does not prove that no repair exists.

families.summary: A bounded search records finite geometric evidence.
families.boundary: Finite evidence does not settle the universal problem.

paper.title: Sharp Solved Families and Constant-Factor Paths in Polynomial Lemniscates
paper.subject: Erdős #1041
paper.question: Which explicit short-path families and critical-value estimates are proved for Erdős #1041, and which of those statements have Lean or Comparator checks?
paper.precis: The paper gives ordinary proofs of the length-less-than-2 conclusion for monic trinomials z^n+a z^m+b, with 1≤m<n and all roots in the open unit disc. It also proves that distinct concyclic zeros in degree n≥3 admit an adjacent chord shorter than 2 in {|f|<1} when their circle radius ρ satisfies 2ρ^n≤1; this alternation proof is not formalised in Lean. For squarefree monic polynomials, if the least critical-value modulus μ is at most 13/25, there is also such a connector. Without a root-location restriction, the scaled result gives a path shorter than (5/2) μ^(1/n) in {|f|<(25/13)μ}. Separate length-area and critical-value estimates give further control. Exact counterexamples show why these ingredients do not yield the unrestricted connector theorem; Erdős #1041 remains open.
paper.owns: the problem-specific exposition for Erdős #1041: ordinary all-degree trinomial paths, bounded-radius concyclic chords, a sharp critical-value mean, subsidiary Lean and Comparator checks, and exact obstructions that prevent promoting those estimates to a general connector theorem
paper.not_authority_for: the validity of claims tagged Lean, which belongs to the cited kernel-checked source, or a solution to Erdős #1041, which remains open
